title: ROOT: Gain root on a satellite user terminal by defeating secure boot (Starlink method)
text: Decomposition of the Wouters 2022 Starlink user-terminal attack (see inc-starlink-ut-faultinjection-2022). Objective: run attacker-controlled firmware on the terminal by defeating its software root of trust with a hardware fault. Steps: characterize the boot chain, build a low-cost glitcher, induce a timed voltage fault to bypass the secure-boot signature check, then load unsigned firmware. Teaching point: a software root of trust falls to a hardware fault unless the boot is glitch-resistant.
source: Lennert Wouters, 'Glitched on Earth by Humans', Black Hat USA 2022.

title: Characterize the terminal boot chain and SoC
text: Sub-step. Obtain a terminal, identify the SoC, locate the boot ROM and the secure-boot stage, and find the power rail to glitch. Deterministic check: the secure-boot verification step and a glitchable power/clock target are identified.

title: Build a low-cost voltage fault-injection mod chip
text: Sub-step. Fabricate an inexpensive (about 25 USD) custom board that drives a precisely timed voltage glitch onto the terminal. Deterministic check: the glitcher can deliver a repeatable fault aligned to the boot signature-check window.

title: Voltage-glitch the boot to bypass the secure-boot signature check
text: Sub-step and the core trick. Inject the timed fault so the signature check is skipped or mis-evaluated, breaking the chain of trust. Deterministic check: the boot proceeds past signature verification with an unsigned image present.

lifecycle.text: glitch-resistant secure boot and signed firmware

title: Load and run unsigned attacker firmware (root)
text: Sub-step. With verification defeated, boot a modified image and obtain a root shell for further research. Deterministic check: unsigned firmware executes and grants privileged access.

title: ROOT: Compromise a SATCOM terminal via firmware backdoor and unauthenticated update (Santamarta method)
text: Decomposition of the Santamarta/IOActive SATCOM terminal findings (see inc-santamarta-satcom-backdoors). Objective: gain control of a SATCOM terminal by exploiting backdoors, hardcoded credentials, and an unauthenticated remote-update path. Steps: extract firmware, find the backdoor/credentials, trigger a privileged action via a crafted message, and persist by installing attacker firmware.

title: Obtain and reverse-engineer terminal firmware
text: Sub-step. Acquire the terminal firmware image and analyze it. Deterministic check: firmware extracted and disassembled to the point of identifying auth and update routines.

title: Identify a backdoor or hardcoded credentials
text: Sub-step. Locate an undocumented backdoor account, hardcoded credential, or insecure protocol in the firmware. Deterministic check: a credential or backdoor entry point is recovered from the image.

lifecycle.text: no hardcoded secrets or backdoors in firmware

title: Trigger a privileged action via a crafted message (e.g. SMS)
text: Sub-step. Send an unauthenticated message that the terminal acts on, such as an SMS that initiates a firmware install. Deterministic check: the terminal performs a privileged action from an unauthenticated message.

title: Install persistent attacker firmware
text: Sub-step. Flash modified firmware so control survives reboot. Deterministic check: attacker code persists across a power cycle.

title: ROOT: Establish covert C2/exfiltration by abusing one-way satellite downlinks (Turla method)
text: Decomposition of the Turla satellite-link abuse (see inc-turla-satc2-2015). Objective: receive C2/exfil traffic anonymously by riding an unencrypted broadcast downlink. Steps: find an unencrypted DVB-S downlink and live subscriber IPs, send victim traffic to those IPs, and passively receive the broadcast replies anywhere in the footprint. No spacecraft is compromised; the insecure link is the vulnerability.

title: Find an unencrypted downlink and active subscriber IPs
text: Sub-step. Survey one-way satellite internet downlinks for unencrypted broadcast traffic and identify IP addresses of legitimate subscribers to impersonate as destinations. Deterministic check: live subscriber IPs are observed on an unencrypted downlink.

title: Send victim traffic to a subscriber IP so replies broadcast over the footprint
text: Sub-step. Direct infected hosts to a chosen subscriber IP; the provider relays replies over the broadcast downlink. Deterministic check: data sent to the subscriber IP is observable on the downlink.

lifecycle.text: encrypted, authenticated links remove the broadcast-abuse channel

title: Passively receive the broadcast downlink from anywhere in the footprint
text: Sub-step. Receive the replies with a cheap satellite dish from any location in the footprint, hiding the true C2 location. Deterministic check: C2 traffic is received passively with no link back to the attacker location.

title: ROOT: Induce a false position/time by spoofing GNSS
text: Decomposition of GNSS spoofing (see inc-gnss-spoofing and inc-gnss-spoofing-realworld). Objective: make a target receiver compute attacker-chosen position or time. Steps: obtain an SDR transmitter and spoofing software, generate and overpower the authentic signals so the receiver locks the fakes, then walk the solution to a chosen value.

title: Obtain an SDR transmitter and GNSS spoofing software
text: Sub-step. Acquire a software-defined radio capable of transmitting in the GNSS band and signal-generation software. Deterministic check: a coherent counterfeit GNSS signal can be transmitted.

title: Generate counterfeit signals and walk the receiver to a chosen solution
text: Sub-step. Transmit counterfeit signals aligned to the constellation, gradually exceed authentic signal power, and then drive the tracked position or time toward the authorized test value. Deterministic check: the receiver tracks the counterfeit signals and its reported position or time follows the intended test trajectory.

metadata.audit_note: Merged capture and carry-off under EX-0014.04; EX-0002 is geofenced execution, not spoofing carry-off.

title: Walk the computed position/time to a chosen value
text: Sub-step. Smoothly drive the spoofed solution to steer the target or shift its clock (e.g. into a geofenced region). Deterministic check: the target's reported position or time follows the attacker's intended trajectory.

metadata.audit_note: Orphaned legacy step; its action is now part of at-gnss-overpower under EX-0014.04.

title: ROOT: Capture sensitive data by passively intercepting satellite broadband downlinks (Pavur method)
text: Decomposition of the Pavur 2020 eavesdropping research (see inc-pavur-satcom-eavesdrop-2020). Objective: recover plaintext from others' satellite broadband sessions using cheap consumer equipment. Steps: point a consumer dish at a GEO broadband satellite, tune to and capture the forward downlink, then reassemble IP traffic and extract plaintext. Listening only; no spacecraft is touched.
source: James Pavur et al., 'Whispers Among the Stars', Black Hat USA 2020.

title: Point a consumer dish at a GEO broadband satellite
text: Sub-step. Use about 300 USD of consumer TV equipment to aim at a geostationary broadband satellite. Deterministic check: a usable downlink signal is acquired.

title: Tune to the forward downlink and capture the stream
text: Sub-step. Lock the forward (downlink) carrier and record the DVB-S stream. Deterministic check: the broadcast stream is captured to disk.

title: Reassemble IP traffic and extract plaintext
text: Sub-step. Parse the captured stream back into IP flows and pull out plaintext credentials, sessions, and operational data. Deterministic check: readable application data is recovered without any key.

title: ROOT: Reach the commanding path of an on-orbit asset via a compromised ground station
text: Decomposition of the NASA Landsat-7 / Terra ground-station interference cases (see inc-nasa-landsat-terra-2007). Objective: from a compromised ground station, reach the spacecraft commanding interface. Steps: compromise the ground station or its connection, pivot to the commanding path, and achieve the ability to form accepted commands. Attribution alleged; modeled as a what-if for ground-to-spacecraft trust.
source: 2011 US-China Economic and Security Review Commission report; SoK (tyac008, 2022).

title: Compromise the ground station or its internet connection
text: Sub-step. Gain a foothold on the ground-station systems or the commercial connection they rely on. Deterministic check: code execution or session on a ground-station host.

title: Pivot to the spacecraft commanding interface
text: Sub-step. From the ground network, reach the system that uplinks commands, acting as a legitimate ground station. Deterministic check: the commanding interface is reachable from the foothold.

lifecycle.text: authenticated commanding resists rogue ground stations

title: Achieve the ability to form accepted commands
text: Sub-step. Reach the point where valid commands could be issued to the spacecraft (the reported outcome: all steps required to command were achieved). Deterministic check: a well-formed command is accepted by the (emulated) spacecraft command handler.

lifecycle.text: authenticated telecommand links resist injected commands
